An unregistered target name fails loudly.
The API rejects a name not registered on this
assignment with a 4xx naming it and listing
the registered ones, and the library raises
rather than swallowing it, so the instructor's
test run fails. A typo that silently succeeds
would mean feedback appearing on a target she
meant to exclude, with nothing to explain it.

The guard is set here, and only here in
IMMEDIATE mode.** Without it, an instructor
re-running the autograder to debug something
would re-bill every target on the submission.

Why Phase 2 fails, and whether retrying helps.
Transient, worth a retry inside this run:
1. Rate limiting. Every submission for the
assignment uses ONE instructor API key, and
everyone submits in the last hour before the
deadline. A burst of concurrent containers
on one key makes 429 the expected case.
4. Context overflow on an enormous submission.
5. Model refuses, or returns unparseable output.
6. The container hits the platform's autograder
timeout, in which case nothing runs at all
and the defensive write is what survives.
Note that 1 and 6 are CORRELATED WITH THE
DEADLINE, so the failure rate is not uniform. It
spikes exactly when the most students are
affected. That is the strongest argument for
preferring NIGHTLY in a large course, and an
argument for serialising rather than fanning out
